title: V3B Microtopic Library Package — PROPOSED
description: Structural exchange proposal only. State labels do not authorize acceptance; references, semantics, review authority and curriculum support require separate validation.

role.description: What the step does to the state. A DECLARE step fixes a convention or a domain and legitimately produces no computation; a TRANSFORM step changes the mathematical state and must show the changed state, not describe it; a VERIFY step checks a result against something already established.

numeric.description: The answer's headline result as a structured candidate, so a subject validator can actually check it. A value stated only inside prose is not machine-checkable, and dropping the check because the value is unstructured would silently discard the oracle.

mathml.description: Restricted presentation MathML for this relation, so a product can render it without re-authoring.

gate_relation_ref.description: The engineering gate relation this is a bound copy of. Subject truth is owned by the gate registry; the library holds a copy so the compiler can reach it, and that copy is checked against the owner.

extensions.description: Namespaced subject extensions; no scientific authority is inferred.

scene_instances.description: Concrete figures satisfying this representation. Everything above states what a figure of this kind must show; an instance states one actual figure, bound to the data it draws, so the library can compile a figure instead of only requiring one.

cores.description: Which learner products this figure appears in.

microtopic_ref.description: The microtopic this figure carries. Its obligation is what the compiled figure block is bound to, so a figure can never float free of the teaching it serves.

datum_refs.description: The data records this figure draws. A renderer may only draw values named here.

scene.description: The scene passed to the subject's renderer. Beyond kind, frame and caption the engine enumerates nothing: a renderer declares its own requirements, and a schema that listed them here would have to be edited for every new representation.

verification.description: Optional. Names a subject validator family and binds its inputs to datum ids. Absence means no oracle exists, not that the answer is wrong. Additional keys are subject-declared preconditions, passed through to the validator unchanged.

extensions.description: Namespaced subject extensions; no scientific authority is inferred.

datum.description: A governed quantitative or symbolic value a product may bind to. Without this, the numbers a lesson uses live in a build script and the library cannot drive production. A datum carries its own provenance; it is evidence, not decoration.

extensions.description: Namespaced subject extensions; no scientific authority is inferred.

kind.description: DATUM carries a number with a unit; EQUATION carries a restricted presentation-MathML string.

value.description: A finite number for DATUM, a MathML string for EQUATION.

unit.description: Required for DATUM. A number without a unit is not a governed physical value.

locator.description: Where this value came from: a source location, or an explicit author-created marker.
